vulnerabilities.description: Access token fetched but never used in subsequent API call. Token from getAccessTokenSilently() is awaited but not passed in fetch headers, breaking authentication.
vulnerabilities.code:
const token = await getAccessTokenSilently();
// token is never used in the fetch() call below
vulnerabilities.impact: API calls may succeed without proper authentication; security model bypassed for evidence upload endpoint

vulnerabilities.description: Access token fetched via getAccessTokenSilently() but never included in fetch headers for /api/chat endpoint.
vulnerabilities.impact: Chat API endpoint may not validate user identity properly; authentication enforcement bypassed
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Include token in fetch headers: headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${token}`, ...headers }

vulnerabilities.description: Token fetch attempted but token variable is never used in subsequent API request
vulnerabilities.impact: County validation endpoint lacks proper authentication; rate limiting and user tracking disabled
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Pass token in Authorization header for county validation endpoint

vulnerabilities.description: Token fetch attempt present but token never used. Payment creation endpoint requires proper authentication.
vulnerabilities.impact: Critical: Payment API endpoint may process requests without user verification; potential for unauthorized payment intents
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Include token in all payment API calls: headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${token}`, ...}

vulnerabilities.description: getAccessTokenSilently() called but token never used in fetch to /api/documents/generate
vulnerabilities.impact: Document generation (payment-gated) may not properly authenticate users; potential access control bypass
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Include token in Authorization header for generate endpoint

vulnerabilities.description: Token-fetching pattern visible but incomplete in component initialization flow
vulnerabilities.impact: Potential authentication bypass in editor operations
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Verify all API calls in EditorView include proper Authorization headers

vulnerabilities.description: File type validation relies only on MIME type checking. MIME type can be spoofed by renaming files.
vulnerabilities.impact: Malicious files could bypass client-side validation by spoofing MIME types; relies on server-side magic byte verification
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Code mentions 'magic-byte sniff' in comments - verify server-side validation in lib/api/services.ts is enforced

vulnerabilities.description: 25MB file size limit may be insufficient for large document scans and could lead to storage exhaustion
vulnerabilities.impact: Storage exhaustion attacks possible; no per-user quota visible in client code
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Implement server-side per-user storage quotas and rate limiting on uploads

vulnerabilities.description: ReactMarkdown component renders content without explicit HTML sanitization configuration
vulnerabilities.impact: If TERMS_OF_SERVICE content source is compromised, arbitrary HTML/JS could execute
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Add sanitization config: disallowedElements={['script', 'iframe', 'object']}, defaultChecked sanitizer like DOMPurify

vulnerabilities.description: Custom tooltip parsing with {{term}} syntax - while safer than dangerouslySetInnerHTML, relies on TOOLTIP_DEFINITIONS being secure
vulnerabilities.impact: Low risk due to React's built-in escaping, but TOOLTIP_DEFINITIONS source should be audited
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Verify TOOLTIP_DEFINITIONS in lib/content/termsOfService.js contains no user-supplied content

vulnerabilities.description: Complex authentication flow with ref-based duplicate redirect prevention. Race condition possible between SDK state changes.
vulnerabilities.impact: Potential infinite login loops or missed TOS validation under concurrent updates
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Simplify state management using a single source of truth; consider moving TOS check to server-side middleware

vulnerabilities.description: TOS acceptance status stored in localStorage with user.sub as key: localStorage.getItem(`tos_accepted_${user?.sub}`)
vulnerabilities.impact: Low: Users can clear localStorage to re-see TOS, but server-side TOS status in database is authoritative
vulnerabilities.recommendation: This is acceptable as long as server validates tosAccepted status on every auth check. Verify /api/auth/tos-status endpoint enforces this.

vulnerabilities.description: Error details logged to console and potentially sent to monitoring service with stack traces
vulnerabilities.impact: Low in production (assuming window.logError is a trusted service), but error details exposed in dev console
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Sanitize component stack traces before sending to monitoring; avoid exposing file paths in production logs

vulnerabilities.description: Hardcoded supported states list in component; changes require code modification
vulnerabilities.impact: Low: This is a frontend convenience list, not a security boundary. API should enforce supported jurisdictions server-side.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Fetch SUPPORTED_STATES from /api/templates/states; verify API enforces jurisdiction restrictions

vulnerabilities.description: Stripe publishable key used in client (NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY is intentionally public), but secret key handling must be server-side
vulnerabilities.impact: Low: Publishable keys are meant to be public. Verify secret key is NEVER in client code.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Audit all .env files and ensure STRIPE_SECRET_KEY only appears in server-side code

vulnerabilities.description: Token obtained but not used - while not a direct vulnerability, suggests incomplete auth integration
vulnerabilities.impact: Inconsistent authentication pattern; may indicate multiple bugs across components
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Search codebase for all getAccessTokenSilently() calls and verify each is used in corresponding API request

recommendations.title: URGENT: Fix Authentication Token Usage in API Calls
recommendations.description: Multiple components fetch access tokens but never use them. This breaks the authentication model for evidence upload, chat, payment, and document generation endpoints. Create a utility function to consistently add Authorization headers.

recommendations.title: Add HTML Sanitization to ReactMarkdown Components
recommendations.description: TermsOfServiceModal uses ReactMarkdown without sanitization config. Add explicit sanitization to prevent XSS if content source is compromised.

recommendations.title: Verify Server-Side File Upload Validation
recommendations.description: Client-side MIME type validation can be spoofed. Ensure server-side magic byte validation exists in lib/api/services.ts for evidence files.

recommendations.title: Implement Server-Side Storage Quotas
recommendations.description: No per-user storage quotas visible in client code. Implement server-side limits to prevent storage exhaustion attacks.

recommendations.title: Simplify TOSGuard Authentication Flow
recommendations.description: Complex state management with ref-based guards creates race condition risk. Move TOS validation to server-side middleware or use simpler client state pattern.

recommendations.title: Create Consistent Auth Headers Utility
recommendations.description: Build a reusable `makeAuthenticatedRequest()` utility that automatically attaches tokens to all API calls.

recommendations.title: Audit .env Files for Secret Key Exposure
recommendations.description: Verify STRIPE_SECRET_KEY and other secrets never appear in client-bundled code. Check .env.local, .env.example, and build artifacts.

recommendations.title: Sanitize Error Logs Before External Transmission
recommendations.description: Remove sensitive information (file paths, stack traces) before sending errors to monitoring services.

strengths: Parameterized SQL queries via pg library - SQL injection risk LOW
RLS (Row-Level Security) enforced at database level
Relative URLs in API calls prevent CORS bypasses
Proper use of TypeScript for type safety in Route Handlers
weaknesses: Inconsistent authentication token usage across components
Client-side validation as primary security boundary in some cases
Complex state management in auth flows increases bug likelihood
Limited error sanitization in error boundary
No visible rate limiting configuration on client

complianceNotes.dataProtection: TOS acceptance tracking exists but localStorage-based; server-side enforcement critical
complianceNotes.authentication: Auth0-based with good RLS policies, but token usage inconsistency weakens model
complianceNotes.fileHandling: 25MB limit reasonable for documents; magic-byte validation required server-side
complianceNotes.paymentProcessing: Stripe integration appears compliant; secret keys must never be client-side

analysisMethod: Manual code review of client components and API routes with focus on authentication, file handling, and data validation patterns
